records.text: An American lieutenant colonel was pictured on the Mexican side after the tunnel apparently had been built, along with Mexican and U.S. military personnel; Mitch said this indicated there had been some collaboration
records.speaker: Mitch Snow

appearances.snippet: One of the commanders that was with the border patrol was actually posed with a photo that was done on the Mexican side after the tunnel apparently had been built along with other Mexican military and U.S. military. So there had been some collaboration.

verification.notes: Historical reporting confirms that the 1990 tunnel prompted speculation about collaboration on the U.S. side, and federal prosecutors later established the cartel architect's role. But no reviewed source authenticates the alleged photograph, identifies an American lieutenant colonel in it, dates it to post-construction, or establishes collaboration by the pictured military personnel. The personal account and its inference remain attempted/unverifiable.

records.text: A Tucson-based Thomas Martin is reportedly a U.S. Border Patrol director and U.S. Southern Command chief of staff, though the tip may not pan out.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #4 (Ep 4YgrOhhy708)

appearances.snippet: And I'm going to say this is a lead. ... I'm going to cage this. It's a possibility that this does not pan out. ... but it's potentially explosive. There is a director of U.S. Border Patrol, ... also chief of staff. ... Staff of the Southern Command in Tucson named Thomas Martin.

verification.notes: The episode accurately presents this as an anonymous, uncertain tip. An official DHS task-force roster identifies a Thomas Martin in Tucson-sector border work as an Arizona Counter-Terrorism Task Force deputy chief of staff, not as a U.S. Southern Command chief of staff; USNORTHCOM identifies the Fort Huachuca border command as Joint Task Force-Southern Border under Northern Command. The tip appears to conflate distinct organizations and titles.

records.speaker: Candace Owens

verification.notes: The episode shows search-result remnants attributed to LinkedIn and ZoomInfo. Those exact profiles were not independently recoverable, but an official DHS roster corroborates a Thomas Martin serving in Tucson-sector border operations and as an Arizona Counter-Terrorism Task Force deputy chief of staff. It does not establish that this is the same individual as the 1985 agent or support the extracted U.S. Southern Command framing.

records.text: A 1985 newspaper article reported that Border Patrol agent Thomas Martin warned that entering sanctuary churches would be used to portray the U.S. government as breaking down church doors.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: a lawsuit and the content of this lawsuit is impressive. This is an old newspaper article again from October 20. ... 21st 1985 it appeared in the times union and it says the sanctuary movement is on trial it tells us the story of this guy who um picked up a hitchhiker and there a movement was born and to begin smuggling humans across the border and hiding them into churches i kid you not ... essentially the argument that he's making is we actually shouldn't invade these churches because then it's going to become a talking point that oh look at the big bad like you know ice agents that are invading churches and we shouldn't do that so i'm going to direct quote because he testified and he said um he wrote to his superiors quote a ploy is going to be border patrol baiting in order to demonstrate to the public that the u.s government thinks nothing of breaking down the doors of their churches

verification.notes: A scholarly legal-history article reproduces and cites the 1985 Thomas Martin memorandum warning that sanctuary activists could portray Border Patrol action as the government breaking down church doors. The wording and historical attribution materially match the statement.

sources.title: University of St. Thomas Law Journal: Operation Sojourner
sources.relevance: Scholarly article reproducing and citing Thomas Martin's 1985 memorandum.

records.text: Harry Myers alleged that photographs in the Mexican-side tunnel house showed U.S. military and Border Patrol personnel posing with El Chapo and a tunnel architect
records.speaker: Harry Myers

appearances.snippet: where our Joint Task Commander, who was a high-ranking Border Patrol, was actually in the photos in that house posing with El Chapo and Felipe (architect; surname unverified), his architect, and there were other U.S. Marine officers and Mexican law enforcement officers and military that were in those photos, okay, end quote.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous tunnel reporting confirms the house, tunnel, JTF-6 detection team, and raid, but searches found no published photographs or official inventory matching the described images. Because the transcript is Owens reading Myers account, the speaker and conveyance were corrected and the image claim retained explicitly as his allegation.
